# Known at-exit leaks under AddressSanitizer (#1279). Generated by:
#   make test-asan          # tees the run to /tmp/asan_output.txt
#   scripts/check_asan_leaks.py --write-baseline <this file> /tmp/asan_output.txt
#
# One line per leak ORIGIN, keyed <file>::<function> from the first stack
# frame that is our code. Only DIRECT leaks are keyed — an indirect leak is a
# child of a direct one, and counting both double-counts the same defect.
#
# Line numbers are deliberately absent, template argument lists are truncated
# to their first argument, parameter lists are dropped, and Catch2 test
# numbering is normalized away. All four move for reasons that have nothing to
# do with the leak, and a key that moves is a baseline nobody trusts. See the
# rationale in scripts/check_asan_leaks.py.
#
# A key NOT listed here fails the build. The list may SHRINK as leaks are
# fixed; it must not grow. Regenerate rather than hand-editing.
#
# The ceilings below catch an already-listed origin leaking MORE, which the key
# set alone cannot see. They come from the SUMMARY line, so they cover direct
# and indirect bytes together.
max-leaked-bytes: 102253
max-leaked-objects: 760

include/observer_factory.h::observe_int_sync<helix::PrintStatusWidget>
